links.note: OVERWRITE of 31592 'The simplest answer', which is the general reply that the mountain is there. The item asks for the author's PERSONAL answer - drawn to mountains since childhood and miserable away from them - which is 31593.
OVERWRITE of 31600 'Inspiration for life's ordeals', which is what Everest gave him afterwards. Endurance, persistence and will power are named in 31592 as what overcoming such obstacles demands.
OVERWRITE of 31606 'Buds nipped and blossoms blown', which is the closing appeal to the parents. School driving all joy away opens the caged-bird section of the poem, 31605.

OVERWRITE of 31592 'The simplest answer', which belongs to the prose lesson, not the poem. 'Nor in my book can I take delight, nor sit in learning's bower' is part of the school-misery stanzas held as 31605.
